As part of a stack of PRs building toward #38631 (induced copy counts), I noticed an inconsistency in Copy.lean worth discussing before the ll→l rename in #38745 locks in another layer of deprecated aliases. Currently:

  • labeledCopyCount H G is the count of labeled copies Copy H G
  • copyCount H G is the count of unlabeled copies {G' : G.Subgraph // Nonempty (H ≃g G'.coe)}

So for types, the labeled notion has no prefix; for counts, the unlabeled notion has no prefix; opposite conventions. Probably worth aligning these before adding more names to the pile. Happy to make whatever changes are preferred — just not sure which direction makes most sense here, and it seems like a decision worth making explicitly rather than inheriting by accident. Since SimpleGraph is inherently labeled in mathlib (while blackboard convention in my experience usually treats "graph" as unlabeled), it might make sense to make labeled notion the one that is prefix-free? One issue is that regardless of which one picks, there is currently no way to change it without breaking either what Copy or what copyCount means.

Christoph Spiegel said:

So for types, the labeled notion has no prefix; for counts, the unlabeled notion has no prefix; opposite conventions.

Wdym by "types" here? docs#SimpleGraph.Copy itself? Are you suggesting LabeledCopy?

As for the counts, I think prefixing both is a good option, labeledCopyCount / unlabeledCopyCount

They type(s) of "a copy of a graph in another graph"; Copy H G in the labeled case and the unnamed subtype {G' : G.Subgraph // Nonempty (H ≃g G'.coe)} in the unlabeled case (assuming everyone is onboard with the move away from the set {G' : G.Subgraph | Nonempty (H ≃g G'.coe)} in #38931).
I would be happy with prefixing both, bc I have definitely in the past stumbled over the fact that copyCount is not counting unlabeled copies.

The question is whether {G' : G.Subgraph // Nonempty (H ≃g G'.coe)} should even be named (I would be in favor of it because to me it is the slightly more relevant or natural notion) and if so, if we should mirror the naming convention from {unlabeled,labeled}CopyCount?
Why do you want to name this set/subtype? It seems like an implementation detail of the counting method, and not something you want to expose in theorem statements

There is definitely applications in Turan / Ramsey theory where at least my intuition would be to make statements over the unlabeled copies (i.e. sets) rather than labeled ones (i.e. injections). But maybe I haven't properly adjusted to the mathlib way of thinking here. A more silly reason is that this rather unwieldy term appears three times in Copy.lean and it seemed reasonable to name it there to avoid the repetition and give the more blackboard-ish notion a proper name. I also have a future PR planned that connects the two count notions through the number of graph automorphisms, but I don't think that really requires naming it explicitly either. So no particularly pressing reason. Keeping Copy as is and not naming the unlabeled one, but distinguishing both counts through a clear prefix seems sensible to me.
I think it's worth revisiting this set after the vertex-sets refactor, since we'll no longer have Subgraphs so the labeled/unlabeled subtypes could be subtypes of the same type (SimpleGraph), I think
Didn't know about the vertex-sets refactor, is there already a PR or some discussion? Would be very interested in seeing what is planned. found it
Regardless, would it make sense to update #38745 to enforce a prefix for {labeled,unlabeled}CopyCount?
I think so, but perhaps we should wait for more opinions

I'd personally prefer Copy, copyCount, etc. rely on the definition of Copy as an injective homomorphism and refer to labeled copies. (The original intention of this file was to separate Copy from Extremal/basic.lean.)

Then unlabeled copies as unlabeledCopyCount, etc.

I'd actually prefer isoSubgraphCount, isoIndSubgraphCount for the unlabeled definitions instead, as these definitions don't rely on Copy and count isomorphic subgraphs and isomorphic induced subgraphs. (The name would tell you how it is defined.) They could also go in different files to keep copy.lean only related to the unlabeled Copy definitions.

I think omitting labeled and highlighting unlabeled or iso would be the most principled given that SimpleGraph itself is inherently labeled (rather than the blackboard convention of a "graph" referring to an equivalence class). But that means there will be a swap-over where copyCount changes from unlabeled to labeled that cannot be transitioned with a deprecated alias. Not sure how much of a no-no that is for mathlib? @Snir Broshi's explicit prefix suggestion seems to be the only way to avoid that while making things consistent.

Looking at this more broadly, the underlying notion is that of a homomorphism, i.e., a map V G → V H that preserves adjacency. In terms of qualifies, there are ...

  • two axes that qualify the map (injectivity and surjectivity),
  • one axis that qualifies the adjacency preservation (inducedness, i.e., upgrading → to ↔), and
  • one axis that quotients Hom G H by precomposition with Aut G.

Denoting the 16 possible combinations through a "character" with four positions ↔ I S / for (in order) strong, injective, surjective, and quotient by Aut, I believe the following summarizes the landscape:

relevance character SimpleGraph blackboard refs
●●● ···· Hom A B / →g homomorphism, hom(H,G), t(H,G) [HN04, Lov12, Lov67, BCLSV06, Sid93]
○○○ ···/ — homomorphism type / hom up to relabelling —
●●● ·I·· Copy A B, labelledCopyCount labelled copy / injective hom / monomorphism, inj(H,G), t_inj(H,G) [HN04]
●●● ·I·/ inlined, copyCount (unlabelled) copy / subgraph isomorphic to A, sub(H,G) [HN04]
●●○ ↔··· — strong / full / induced hom (HN04: "full") [BNP10, HN04, HT97]
●○○ ↔··/ — strong-hom type [Spi+22]
●●● ↔I·· Embedding A B / ↪g (induced) embedding / strong monomorphism, emb(H,G) [HN04]
●●● ↔I·/ — induced subgraph isomorphic to A, ind(H,G), t_ind(H,G) [PG75, BNT86, BS94, Raz07]
●●○ ··S· — surjective hom / epimorphism [PT80, Nes06, FS13, HN04]
○○○ ··S/ — — —
●○○ ·IS· — spanning bijective hom (A iso to spanning subgraph of B) [BM08, Die25]
●●○ ·IS/ — spanning subgraph of B isomorphic to A [KSS97, KO09, BM08, Die25]
●●○ ↔·S· — (graph) quotient / fold [HN92, HN04, HT97, GR01]
○○○ ↔·S/ — — —
●●● ↔IS· Iso A B / ≃g isomorphism (A = B: automorphism), aut(H) for A = B [HN04]
○○○ ↔IS/ — conjugacy class of isomorphisms (≅ a point) —

Note that three of these notions originate from Mathlib.Order.RelIso: Hom A B := RelHom A.Adj B.Adj (carries →g notation), Embedding A B := RelEmbedding A.Adj B.Adj (carries ↪g), and Iso A B := RelIso A.Adj B.Adj (carries ≃g).

List of references (admittedly accumulated with Claude).

The question is whether to work additively, that us fill in the relevant gaps (what #38631 tries to do) and fix inconsistencies (what we are discussing here), or to refactor exhaustively with some heavily prefixed system like {Strong}{Inj}{Surj}{Aut}Hom. They could also be combined, i.e., common notions have blackboard-aligned aliases but everything is based on an exhaustive system.

For the additive approach, a sensible set would probably be (besides the existing Hom for ···· and Iso A B for ↔IS· that do not need count versions) the following additions or modifications for the existing and the planned induced notions:

  • Copy{Count,Density} for ·I·· which breaks the current usage of copyCount and deprecateslabelledCopyCount.
  • Sub{Count,Density} for ·I·/ where Sub is currently inlined as a subset- instead of subtype-based notation and subCount would replace the (now re-assigned) copyCount. Note the potential clash with SimpleGraph.Subgraph which I tried to avoid with the shortened Sub to align with Hom.
  • IndSub{Count,Density} for ↔I·/.
  • Embedding{Count,Density} for ↔I··. If we wanted to be principled we could also use / alias the short form Emb here.

Additionally, one could eventually also add:

  • count and density for Hom, i.e., ···.
  • StrongHom{Count,Density} for ↔···.
  • Epi{Count,Density} for ··S·.
  • Fold{Count,Density} for ↔·S·

There is also an argument that the default in mathlib is "labeled" (see SimpleGraph whose vertices V are inherently labeled) and we only need to highlight the unlabeled case.
